summary: Bodies keep one identity through the features that change them. src/domain/cad/cadBodies.ts derives the bodies after each feature from the history and each kind's declared body behaviour. A body is keyed by the feature that created it, plus an occurrence where that feature makes a copy or a piece: inst(i,j) for a pattern copy, split(k) for a piece of a split body and mirror for a mirror image. A feature that modifies a body (fillet, chamfer, shell, move, cut, join, pocket and the patterns) keeps its key and is recorded in modifiedBy. A Boolean keeps its target's key and records itself as consumedBy on each tool. Each state is { key, kind, createdBy, modifiedBy, consumedBy?, pieces?, ambiguous?, interchangeable?, untracked? }. Validation and the kernel resolve a stored target through this lineage, strictly by the feature whose result the body now is, as before, so every diagnostic is unchanged. The kernel keys its bodies by body key and tracks the parts of a body, its split pieces and separate pattern copies, only where continuity is certain. Each solid of a feature's result is traced to every source solid it keeps a face of unchanged: the target's pieces, each pattern copy and a fused tool. A face two solids or two sources share is never traced, since which of them it would count for follows the kernel's order. A solid that continues one target piece keeps its key, a copy is inst(i,j) of the piece copied, and a piece split again is split(q), numbered by the first face it keeps, never by position, size or centroid. Anything else gets a fresh feature/split(k) key, a reported ambiguity or a reported loss, never a guess. Faces rank in the order the kernel lists solids, so ranks order solids only when the faces they are numbered by lie in the same solid of one source and differ; solids that equal ranks or the kernel's order would order are ambiguous. A solid keeping no face of the body may be a piece of any of its keys, so it, the keys continued by one solid and the keys no solid continues are ambiguous together. A mirror image starts whole under its own key. Ambiguity is kept in groups and carries to every descendant: the keys descending from one group through one source form a group, an ambiguous key resolves only among the current pieces of its group, and a key ambiguous only by descent extends the issue that reported its ambiguity instead of being reported again, until that issue lists 4,096 keys; the later feature then reports the rest in an issue of its own. Since the kernel's order picked which member's key each solid continued, a group keeps every former member's key, whether its solid split, was copied or went, while a solid descends from the group through the target, and a key no body lists resolves as ambiguous when another kernel order would have given it a solid. A body records in interchangeable, per split, the siblings whose order the kernel decided: pieces tied by rank, or ordered by faces of different solids or by none. Every later step follows its solid, so the keys other orders would have given are the key with any of its steps, read from the first, changed to a sibling in that step's set, never a sibling that only inherited a group, a copy, an image or a later feature's key with the same steps. A body tracks at most 4,096 distinct part keys, its pieces, the keys its groups keep and the keys its interchangeable sets keep, together; past that its parts are untracked for the rest of the history. A consumed body's ambiguous keys resolve as missing with the Boolean that consumed it. CadBuildResult.bodyIssues reports each feature's ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts and untracked-body-parts, with more-body-issues past 512: a hook D1 can adopt. Every build returns the body states (CadBuildResult.bodies, CadMesh.bodyKey), and the worker reply check verifies them against the meshes. Consumers choose bodies by key: a command started with a feature selected (Fillet, Chamfer, Move, the patterns, Mirror, Pocket and the target of a Boolean) and File > Section for CAM now act on the body that feature leads to, wherever it sits in that body's history, instead of falling back to the latest body. The DXF export dialog's initial body is chosen the same way, by key first, and cad_build rows add bodyKey. Stored targets still hold feature ids and nothing stored changes. S8's CadBodyRef and CadBodyMetadata shapes and their resolution are defined and tested but not stored. docs/maintainers/cad-features.md describes body identity.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. The CAD document and edit schemas, agent tool schemas and descriptions, parsed documents, diagnostics, kernel geometry, sections, STL exports and saved bytes in the browser cache and folder adapters are identical to main at 9b236720 (0.0.796), this change's base. Two additive changes are visible. cad_build body rows gain a bodyKey field beside featureId, which agents may ignore; tools still take featureId as bodyId. With a feature selected that is no longer the latest state of its body, such as a pad that was later filleted, starting Fillet, Chamfer, Move, a pattern, Mirror, Pocket or a Boolean, or opening File > Section for CAM, now targets that pad's body in its filleted state instead of the most recently changed body.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage or journal change. The published CAD document schema, edit schema and every feature variant are byte-identical. Body keys are derived on every rebuild and never stored; stored target, source and tool fields still hold feature ids. The worker build reply gains optional bodies, bodyIssues and CadMesh.bodyKey fields. The main thread and the worker ship together, and the reply check accepts a reply without them, as older build results are. When present, it requires one body state per mesh, in mesh order, whose key is the mesh's bodyKey, whose current feature is the mesh's featureId and whose pieces, when present, key the mesh's solids one for one with no key repeated, whose ambiguous groups, when present, are non-empty and share no key, and whose interchangeable sets, when present, each hold two or more sibling keys under one parent ending in a split step and share no key; it requires unique mesh keys and at most 512 issues. Review round 2 changed ambiguous from a list of keys to a list of groups, and review round 5 adds interchangeable; both are part of the build reply only, which the main thread and the worker ship together, and are never stored. A body tracks at most 4,096 distinct part keys, its pieces, the keys its groups keep and the keys its interchangeable sets keep, together, which the reply check also enforces, an issue lists at most 4,096 keys, and an issue message gives counts, never part keys. A body with more part keys, or a longer part key, is reported as untracked for the rest of the history, so a large valid model is summarised, never refused. Post engine API remains 1, saved-job engine remains 3 and CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 2. S8's CadBodyRef and CadBodyMetadata are types and resolution functions only.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation, input-version or WebMCP guard change. Initial CAD discovery stays at 51,178 of its 51,200 UTF-8 bytes: no tool name, description or input schema changes. cad_describe_features and cad_describe_edits return byte-identical replies. cad_build body rows add bodyKey, the creating feature id with any occurrence (such as flip/mirror), after featureId; docs/site/agents.md explains it. Every diagnostic code and message is unchanged. The only new codes, ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts, untracked-body-parts and more-body-issues, are body issues returned in bodyIssues, never diagnostics.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls. Commands started with a feature selected now choose that feature's body by key; with no selection, or a selection that leads to no drawn body, they choose the latest body as before. The Boolean tool default is the latest other body, as before.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Kernel geometry, mesh order, previews, sections and STL exports are byte-identical. STEP export writes the same bodies in the same order under the same names, the feature names, until S8 stores body metadata.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Every parity document loads, validates, rebuilds and saves to identical bytes through both the browser cache and folder adapters.

Since review round 1. All five findings are fixed in aa2696b9 under one rule: a key is inherited only when continuity is certain; anything else gets a fresh key, a reported ambiguity or a reported loss, never a guess. createCadKernelFaceSources replaces cadKernelSolidOrigins and records the faces of every source a feature combines (the target's solids, each pattern copy before it is released, and a fused tool); cadBodyParts gives each result solid its key from the source solids it keeps faces of. occurrences is removed: pattern copies are traced per solid into pieces. ambiguous-split-order is replaced by ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts, untracked-body-parts and more-body-issues. (1) A valid build failed the worker check because the ambiguity message listed every key (9,721 characters). Messages now give counts and keep the keys in pieces; lists hold at most 4,096 keys, past which a body is reported untracked; issues stop at 512 with a summary; modifiedBy stays uncapped and checked by entry; and the reply check requires pieces to key the mesh's solids one for one. 100 copies of a cleaved rod created by a 36-character UUID id give 200 ambiguous keys, a 123-character message and a reply that passes the check. (2) An island joined beside a split box inherited a piece's key by elimination. Every solid is now traced to every predecessor it keeps faces of: the island gets bridge/split(0), the bridged solid bridge/split(1), and both box pieces are reported lost and resolve as missing. (3) A pocket in one piece of a cleaved cylinder erased its ambiguity. Ambiguity now carries to every descendant, and the pieces stay ambiguous candidates. (4) A pattern copy cut away still resolved. Copies are traced per solid, so the cut reports box/inst(1,0) lost and it resolves as missing. (5) A cut that split one patterned cube and removed the other went unseen because the count did not change. Splits and losses are found per predecessor solid, never by totals; the repro gives box/inst(0,0)/split(0) and split(1) and reports box/inst(1,0) lost. Each repro is a kernel test, and a property test over random histories (10 seeds of 5 steps from a box or disc, drawing patterns, one- to three-slot splits, cuts, one- or two-profile joins and pockets) checks at every step that no key repeats, that each piece keeps or extends a key from before or is a fresh key of the step's feature, that a solid inheriting a key without ambiguity overlaps its predecessor, that ambiguity is reported and inherited, that no piece vanishes unreported, that every reported loss resolves as missing then and later, and that rebuilds are identical. The kernel gives kept faces cheaply but not faces a Boolean's simplification merges: an extruded circle's two half side faces are merged by a pattern's fuse, so the copies of round hole and boss patterns keep no face and get fresh, ambiguous keys instead of guessed ones until K3 provides the Boolean's own face history. Parity after round 1 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, against main at 5ab4b5ea and again after the merge against main at 9b236720; derived body states or issues changed from round 0 in 18 of the 86 documents, all as the rule requires. S5 (0.0.796, #111) is on main as 9b236720 and f99219ca merges it, keeping 0.0.797 with previousVersion 0.0.796. Only the version fields of package.json and package-lock.json conflicted; CadWorkbench.tsx, its test and docs/site/agents.md merged cleanly, and on the merged tree the body states and issues equal those before the merge. Since review round 2. All six findings are fixed in d68b4cf2, and nothing stored changes. (1) A mirror image took its source's piece order as certain: reversing the first cleave's solid order moved flip/mirror/split(0) to another piece of a cleaved, patterned, mirrored and cut cylinder. Faces rank within their source in the order the kernel lists its solids, so ranks now order solids only when the faces they are numbered by lie in the same solid of one source. A mirror image still starts whole under its own key; when a later feature splits it, the pieces numbered by faces of different solids of the image are ambiguous, and the piece keeping no face of it is numbered last in either order. It does not carry its source's pieces: mapping source keys onto image keys would be a second naming scheme, and the rank rule already refuses any order the kernel decides. (2) Incomplete face provenance counted as proof: an intersection that kept an end slab and an interior core of the first of two solids left the body whole, and with a patterned target kept box/inst(0,0) certain. A solid keeping no face of the body now counts as a possible split whatever the totals, and as a possible piece of any key, so it, the keys continued by one solid and the keys no solid continues are ambiguous together: the repro reports keep/split(0), box/inst(0,0) and box/inst(1,0) as one group, and a whole two-solid body cut the same way splits into multi/split(0) and multi/split(1). (3) Ambiguous references resolved across pattern occurrences. CadBodyState.ambiguous now holds groups: the keys that descend from one group through one source form a group, and an ambiguous key resolves only among the current pieces of its group, so rod/split(0)/inst(0,0) resolves among its own copy's two pieces. A group's keys that no solid continues stay in it while a solid descends from it through the target, and are lost after, so cutting away one half of the cleaved rod leaves both keys ambiguous to the half left instead of one lost and one certain. (4) Inherited ambiguity was reported again by each later feature. A key ambiguous only because it descends from an ambiguous key now extends the issue that reported that key: 100 copies of the cleaved rod give one cleave issue of 202 keys. (5) Every modifier copied the body's modifier list. Modifiers now link into a history the states share, and modifiedBy is made once, when a state is asked for; validation only asks whether a body exists. (6) The worker check accepted repeated piece keys. It now rejects a key repeated in pieces or across ambiguous groups, an empty group and a flat list, with malformed-reply tests in both suites. The random-history test now also draws mirrors and Boolean intersections with one or two blocks through or inside the body, aims cuts at a single piece and joins across two, runs 16 seeds, and builds every step a second time with the kernel's multi-solid Boolean results listed in reverse: every key must name the same solid, by its box and surface area, in both orders, or be ambiguous in both, and the issues must agree. Parity after round 2 against main at 9b236720 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, and tool metadata stays at 51,178 bytes. Derived body data changed from round 1 in 4 of the 86 documents: plate-40-pattern reports one ambiguity of 50 keys instead of two issues of 10 and 40, and near-full-turn-pattern, split-fillet and split-cylinder keep the same ambiguous keys as one group. Since review round 3. All four findings are fixed in 27c90694, 4bd71755 and d2981d2e, and nothing stored changes. (1) Equal face ranks certified kernel-dependent identities: two adjacent native solids sharing a face, intersected by a slab spanning their boundary, both traced to that face, so reversing the solid order swapped imported/split(0) between x = 8 to 10 and x = 10 to 12. A face that two solids of a source, or two sources, share is now never traced, since which of them it would count for follows the order they are listed in, and solids that equal ranks would order are ambiguous. The repro, built from boxes fused by the builder algorithm, traces no face and is ambiguous in both orders. It is tested at the kernel and domain boundary only, since a STEP round trip did not keep the shared face. (2) Splitting an ambiguous member made its old key missing: after a box split at x = 18 to 20, filleted on every edge and split again at x = 30 to 32, round/split(1) became missing although it could name the unsplit left piece, and reversing the first cut's solid order swapped which key disappeared. Since the kernel's order picked which member's key each solid continued, a group now keeps every former member's key, whether its solid split, was copied or went, while a solid descends from the group through the target. Keeping it only while another member was left unchanged, the first fix, still depended on the order: with splits aimed at ambiguous pieces, the random-history test found a key ambiguous in one order and missing in the other. A key no body lists resolves as ambiguous when its nearest listed ancestor is ambiguous and another member of that ancestor's group has a descendant by the same steps, which another kernel order would have given it. After a pattern, the old keys of an ambiguous group therefore resolve as ambiguous among the original's pieces instead of missing. The either-order helper now requires every key either order lists to resolve with the same status in both, and the generator adds a slot through the middle of an ambiguous piece. (3) Consumed ambiguous keys lost their consumer: a key kept only in its group resolved as plain missing once a Boolean consumed the body. The consumed lookup now includes ambiguous groups and the keys resolved as above, so both halves of a cleaved rod resolve as missing with consumedBy union. (4) The issue limit was not documented. A key ambiguous by descent extends its first issue only until that issue lists 4,096 keys; the later feature reports the rest in an ambiguous-body-parts issue of its own, as the guide, this record and the pull request now say. A domain test runs a comb cut's 1,000 ambiguous teeth through two patterns with a cut between them: the comb's issue fills to 4,096 keys and the second pattern reports the other 904. Parity after round 3 against main at 9b236720 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, and tool metadata stays at 51,178 bytes. Derived body data is the same as after round 2 in all 86 documents, none of which has a case the round 3 rules change. Since review round 4. Both findings are addressed in 64f814f6 and 2b46cc9a, and nothing stored changes. (1) A key could resolve into another pattern generation's solid. A 40 by 20 by 10 box was split at x = 18 to 20, filleted on every edge, split again at x = 30 to 32 and patterned by x = 100; a join bridged the originals and a second pattern copied by y = 50. Reversing only the first cut's solid order made round/split(0)/inst(1,0) resolve among the three pieces at x = 100 to 140 in one order and to the second pattern's bridged solid at y = 50 to 70 in the other, with nothing reported. The twin lookup took the first member of the nearest listed ancestor's group with a descendant by the same steps, here bridge/split(0), which a later feature made. A kernel order decides only which of the keys one split gave at once names which solid; every later step follows its solid, and pattern copies and mirror images are told apart by the faces they keep. So a twin is now the key with one split step changed to a sibling's, a key the same split gave beside it in its group. Key text names no feature, but all of a key's children come from one operation, since a key retires when its solid splits or is copied, so siblings share the operation that derived them. The nearest step with any twin decides, among the groups of all its twins, and a certain piece or the body's own key ends the search. The repro is a kernel test whose builds vary each multi-solid Boolean's order on its own: the normal order, each of the five reversed alone, all but each reversed and all reversed. Every one agrees with the normal build, and both copies' keys resolve to the pieces at x = 100 to 140. Domain cases cover a later feature's copy that is never a twin, a copy's split traded with its split sibling's, a twin from a split further up, twins in two groups and copies sharing a group that are never traded. No other lookup takes a first match by suffix or name: every other key lookup is by exact key or by derivation. The DXF export dialog matched its initial body by key or feature id in one pass and now tries the key first; visible meshes have unique feature ids, so no reachable result changes. The random-history test now shuffles each Boolean's solids on its own, twice per step, instead of reversing every one. The round 3 rule still passes it over 112 seeds, since its case needs an ambiguous split, a split of one ambiguous piece, a pattern, a join across pieces and a second pattern, in that order; the repro and the domain cases catch it. (2) The list limit was not explained. MAX_CAD_BODY_LIST counts a body's pieces and the keys its groups keep together, and groups keep every former member's key while a solid descends from them. So a body of 100 ambiguous solids that loses one piece and splits another at each feature adds two keys a feature, passes 4,096 at the 1,999th such feature and is untracked for the rest of the history. That limit is separate from an issue's 4,096 keys. The guide, this record and the pull request now say so, and a domain test runs the cutoff: 1,998 cuts leave 100 pieces and a group of exactly 4,096 keys, the 1,999th reports untracked-body-parts, and every key then resolves as missing. Collapsing a group's kept keys to a common prefix was not done: removed and merged keys leave no descendant to imply them, so it would at most halve the growth while adding a third way to resolve a key. Parity after round 4 against main at 9b236720 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, and tool metadata stays at 51,178 bytes. Derived body data is the same as after round 3 in all 86 documents; round 4 changes only how references resolve, which the capture does not record. Since review round 5. Both findings are fixed in 5d2e2696 and c003fc96, and nothing stored changes. (1) Inherited ambiguity made every sibling interchangeable. Round 4's box, split at x = 18 to 20, filleted on every edge and split at x = 30 to 32, was cut again at x = 24 to 26. Across all 8 combinations of the three cuts' solid orders, round/split(1)/split(1)/split(0) resolved as ambiguous in some and missing in others, although no order gives that key: the later cut's halves are ordered by their faces but inherited the fillet halves' group, and the twin rule traded any split siblings in a group. Each body now records in CadBodyState.interchangeable, per split, the siblings whose order the kernel decided: pieces tied by rank, or ordered by faces of different solids or by none. Only those trade keys. A key the body does not list resolves through the keys formed by changing any of its steps, from the first, to a sibling in that step's set, among the groups of those the body lists; groups still give a listed key's candidates. A set stays while one of its keys is, or leads to, a piece, a group's key or a key of another set that stays. An oracle, src/domain/cad/__tests__/cadBodyOrders.test.ts, closes the class. It builds generated histories in a model of the kernel's solid order, in which each solid keeps its faces in its own order, a face ranks by its place in its source, a face two solids share is ranked once and never traced, and a fillet follows its input's order. The generator makes cuts that split, nick or remove solids, with faceless pieces and tied ranks now and then, fillets, patterns that fuse copies, and joins that bridge solids or stand apart; 40% of histories follow split, fillet, split, an optional split, pattern, join and pattern. Each Boolean gets three orders of its own, as made, reversed and shuffled: every combination is built while there are at most 81, and otherwise 81 are sampled, including each Boolean's orders alone. After every feature, every key any combination lists, and every key formed from one by changing any of its split indices, must resolve the same way in every combination: the same solid, the same set of solids, or missing in all; the issues must match too. At 9095fba8 it fails 70 of 400 seeds, 64 of them template-shaped; at 5d2e2696 all 400 pass. publicNotes.summary: CAD bodies keep their identity through the features that change them.
changes: With a feature selected, Fillet, Chamfer, Move, the patterns, Mirror, Pocket, Boolean and Section for CAM act on the body that feature belongs to, even after later features changed it.
CAD build results for agents name each body by the feature that created it (bodyKey), which stays the same through later changes.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
